notes: We're back with another round of balance changes, but first, it's time to break some chains! Sylas, the Unshackled, is making his way to the Rift, and he's ready to steal the show (and your ultimate). Meanwhile, we're turning up the heat (sorry, Rumble) on a few champions and items that have been stealing the spotlight. Kalista and Shen are getting some breathing room adjustments for their opponents, while Yasuo, Lucian, and a few other champions are getting a little extra love. We're also making some changes to mage itemization to give you more ways to work your magic, and taking another pass at the jungle to make sure everyone is clearing on a level playing field. And as for Eclipse? Well, its time in the sun might be coming to an end. Let's dive in!
Reminder: content will be released throughout the patch

blocks.title: SYLAS, THE UNSHACKLED
notes: Raised in one of Demacia's lesser quarters, Sylas of Dregbourne has come to symbolize the darker side of the Great City. As a boy, his ability to root out hidden sorcery caught the attention of the notorious mageseekers, who eventually imprisoned him for turning those same powers against them. Having now broken free, Sylas lives as a hardened revolutionary, using the magic of those around him to destroy the kingdom he once served... and his band of outcast mage followers seems to grow by the day.

blades.summary: Kalista has been a little too dominant in Baron Lane, so we're dialing back her early-game pressure to give her opponents more room to fight back.

Viktor has been struggling to make an impact in key moments, so we're shifting some power away from his reliable AoE damage and into his dueling potential and skillshots. This should give him more opportunities to shine when he lands his abilities.

blocks.title: Siphon Power
lines: Initial Damage: 45/60/75/90 + 30% Ability Power → 50/70/90/110 + 40% Ability Power

blocks.title: Hextech Ray
lines: Initial Damage: 75/120/165/210 + 30% Ability Power → 70/115/160/205 + 40% Ability Power
Blastquake Damage: 30/70/110/150 + 60% Ability Power → 20/60/100/140 + 75% Ability Power

blades.summary: With the recent turret changes, Shen has been able to protect his teammates with his ultimate without sacrificing much pressure elsewhere on the map. We're toning down the strength and availability of his protective tools to make those cross-map plays a more meaningful commitment.

Irelia has been dishing out a bit too much damage without investing in Attack Damage items, so we're shifting some of her base damage into Attack Speed and Attack Damage scaling. This should better reward her for building offensive items and reinforce her identity as a blade-dancing fighter.

blocks.title: Ionian Fervor
lines: Attack Speed: 3% - 17% (Based on level) → 11% - 25% (Based on level)
Damage: 25 - 150 (Based on level) + 30% Bonus Attack Damage → 10 - 80 (Based on level) + 20% Bonus Attack Damage

blades.summary: Graves has plenty of damage at his disposal, but he's been struggling to stay in the fight long enough to make use of it. We're giving him some extra durability to help him hold his ground during jungle skirmishes and teamfights, giving him more opportunities to let loose.

Akshan has been having a tough time holding his own in Mid Lane, particularly against mages. We're giving him some extra durability to help him trade more comfortably in lane and find more opportunities to roam and make plays across the map.

Lucian has been struggling to keep up since the latest patch, so we're giving some damage back to his abilities. This should help him pack a stronger punch in the mid and late game and better deliver on his burst-focused playstyle.
Rumble has been losing some steam in Baron Lane, so we're giving him a few buffs across his kit to help him turn up the heat and hold his own against the competition.

blocks.title: Junkyard Titan
lines: Basic attack Magic Damage Ability power ratio: 20% → 25%

blades.summary: Kassadin has been scaling a little too comfortably in high-skill play, and with Rod of Ages getting buffed this patch, we're expecting him to become even stronger. We're getting ahead of that power spike with some nerfs to keep his late-game strength in check.

Yasuo has continued to struggle, so we're giving him some extra durability to help him survive teamfights and boosting his damage while dashing between enemies. These changes should help him make more of an impact in mid- and late-game fights.

blocks.title: Luden's Echo
notes: Mage itemization has been feeling a bit limited, with burn builds dominating at lower skill levels and Magic Penetration builds pulling ahead in high-skill play. We're buffing several underperforming mage items to open up more viable build paths and help different mage playstyles compete on more equal footing.

blocks.title: Discordic Echo
lines: First projectile damage: 75 + 8% Ability Power → 80 + 9% Ability Power
Subsequent projectile damage: 20 + 1.2% Ability Power → 22.5 + 1.4% Ability Power

blocks.title: Liandry's Torment
notes: As mentioned above, burn builds have been performing a little too well. We want Liandry's Torment to remain focused on its passive effects rather than raw Ability Power.

blocks.title: Bulwark of the Mountain
notes: Supports have been earning Gold a little too quickly, especially following the recent support item cost reductions. We're dialing back some of the Gold they gain through support item systems that require minimal investment to keep their overall economy in check.

blocks.title: Eclipse
notes: Eclipse has been shining a little too brightly, becoming a dominant pick for fighters in both Baron Lane and the jungle. We're dialing back some of its power to bring it more in line with other item options.

blocks.title: Goredrinker
notes: Goredrinker has been struggling to keep up with other fighter items, so we're giving it a boost to help it become a more competitive option.

blocks.title: SYSTEMS
notes: Overall, we're happy with how the jungle changes have landed, but a few areas are performing a bit too well. Tank junglers in particular have been clearing camps too efficiently, allowing them to gank frequently without sacrificing much farm. We're slowing down early jungle clears to bring the different jungle classes closer together in power.
We've also seen jungle farming efficiency increase across the board, so we're reducing some of the rewards from Smite to bring overall jungle progression closer to where it was before the overhaul.

blocks.title: Radiant Vow
lines: Fixed Damage blocked while active: 10 ~ 60 + 3000% Healing and Shield Power → 10 ~ 30 + 2000% Healing and Shield Power

blocks.title: Sing With Me
lines: Shield gained: 10% Base Health → 5% Base Health
Healing value: 3% Missing Health → 2% Missing Health

blocks.title: Shifting Debris
lines: Damage: 60 ~ 180 + 40% Bonus Attack Damage + 30% Ability Power + 4% Target’s Max Health → 40 ~ 120 + 30% Bonus Attack Damage + 10% Ability Power + 2% Target’s Max Health

blocks.title: Veiled Counter
lines: Damage dealt every 0.75 seconds: 120 ~ 180 + 30% Bonus Attack Damage + 15% Ability Power → 60 ~ 120 + 30% Bonus Attack Damage + 15% Ability Power

blocks.title: QOL Improvements
lines: Improved the hit sound effects for K/DA Augments.

blocks.title: Battle Arsenal
lines: Fixed an issue where Battle Arsenal would fail to trigger when an enemy target took item damage from multiple champions simultaneously.
